findings.description: The code always iterates 18 times and never checks if infile >> ... succeeded.

malloc and strdup return values are not checked for NULL before dereferencing.
malloc and strdup return values are not checked for NULL before dereferencing.
Using malloc to allocate a C++ type bypasses constructors.
If the file contains fewer than 18 valid records, the code still sorts and prints 18 entries.
Summing three ints without range validation can overflow if inputs are malicious or unexpected.
Opening a relative path can be abused in certain execution contexts.
